key_findings.title: Vote Share Polarization & Consolidation
key_findings.observation: AIMIM vote share grew from 39.17% (2009) to 61.28% (2024), demonstrating complete consolidation of the Muslim voter base. Simultaneously, BJP doubled vote share from 18.64% (2009) to 29.98% (2024), converting Hyderabad into a direct bipolar duel while squeezing Congress and BRS below 8% combined.

key_findings.title: Goshamahal Anomaly (Assembly vs Parliamentary)
key_findings.observation: Goshamahal is the sole non-AIMIM segment where BJP secured a 70,230 lead in 2024 Lok Sabha. However, AIMIM's massive leads in Bahadurpura (135,407) and Chandrayangutta (86,830) comfortably neutralize Goshamahal by a factor of 3.2x.

key_findings.title: Collapse of Third Poles (BRS & Congress)
key_findings.observation: In 2019, TRS (now BRS) and INC held 12.89% combined. In 2024, despite Congress governing the state of Telangana, their parliamentary candidate garnered only 5.83%, indicating tactical voting by anti-BJP electors toward AIMIM.

key_findings.title: Voter Turnout Asymmetry
key_findings.observation: Turnout in old city core segments (Charminar 45.1%, Yakutpura 43.6%) remains 8-12% below Goshamahal (56.4%) and Bahadurpura (52.8%). The low turnout paradox demonstrates that AIMIM wins decisively even with moderate mobilization, presenting untapped growth potential for opposition if turnout spikes above 65%.
